intended_object: The canonical equivalence of categories (pre F G e ↓ f) ≌ (F ↓ f.left). Here `pre F G e : (F ⋙ G ↓ e) ⥤ (G ↓ e)` is the functor between costructured arrow categories and f is an object of G ↓ e. This is what the docstring and name say.
explanation:
An object of the source category is an object (c, F⋙G c → e) of the category F⋙G ↓ e, together with a morphism of G ↓ e from its image under pre to f. Such a morphism amounts to a map F c → f.left whose composite with f.hom is the given map to e. So the object is determined by the pair (c, F c → f.left), which is exactly an object of F ↓ f.left.

The functor sends g to g.hom.left. The inverse sends g to the object (g.left, G.map g.hom ≫ f.hom), together with the morphism g.hom. The unit and counit isomorphisms are both built from identity morphisms, which is correct. The construction makes sense for arbitrary categories and functors, so it is stated in full generality.

The definition is the costructured-arrow (dual) version of `StructuredArrow.preEquivalence`, so it is not a duplicate of an existing declaration.
